summary: Infrastructure Phase 1 (DURABLE REVISION PROCESSING) end-to-end verified. Backend: 8/8 pytest tests pass in 212s against public URL (https://dev-converse.preview.emergentagent.com). POST /api/sessions/{id}/interact now returns in <0.2s with student_turn.status='complete' + ai_turn.status='processing' (kind='pending', empty content); background asyncio task completes reasoning (~55-70s writing, ~55-90s revise) and persists directly via db.sessions.update_one. Concurrent POST while a turn is processing returns HTTP 409 with detail 'A response is already being prepared'. Empty submission still returns 400. Durability confirmed: submit + sleep 80s with NO client connection -> AI turn is status='complete' with populated invitation and single student/ai pair (no duplicates, no lost work). Resubmit-when-idle returns 200 and starts a new processing turn. M1-M14 regression holds through the new flow: intervention.focus='writing' (M5A), scaffolding_control.primary_target present (M11), reader_construction populated (M12), revision_development.applies=False on first writing turn and True after the revise turn (M13), integration_calibration.applies=True with primary_framework populated (M14). The reasoning view correctly EXCLUDES the placeholder AI turn (previous-draft comparison works — the revise turn produced a distinct, focused invitation rather than duplicating the prior one). Interactions/theory_history each grew by exactly 1 per turn. Frontend: ?dev quick-start lands in Student Workspace, submitting a draft flips continue-button to disabled and shows 3 thinking-dot animations, polling delivers the ai-invitation automatically after ~55-70s without any manual refresh, integration-calibration-block (M14) renders inside the Dev Panel. Reconnection UX verified: while a turn was processing, we RELOADED the page and after reload the app immediately re-detected the processing turn (3 thinking-dots visible, continue-button disabled), polling resumed, and the 2nd ai-invitation appeared automatically — no duplicate turns, no lost work. Total conversation ended with 2 student-turn blocks and 2 ai-invitation blocks as expected. The old 60s SSE ingress ceiling that blocked revise turns in iterations 16-19 is gone (POST returns immediately; reasoning finishes in the background regardless of client presence).

minor.issue: Returns 200 rather than 201 for resource creation. Carry-over from all prior iterations; not blocking.

action_items: None blocking. Durable revision processing is working exactly as specified across backend + frontend.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L860-901 (_run_reasoning) — the background task correctly: (1) reloads the session, (2) builds a reason_session that EXCLUDES the placeholder AI turn before invoking _run_engine, (3) reloads fresh again before persistence to avoid clobbering concurrent writes, (4) guards against the placeholder having already been cancelled/finalized (`if ai is None or ai.status != 'processing': return`), (5) on any exception sets status='failed' with empty content atomically via `turns.$.status`. This is a clean and safe implementation. Empirical proof: after 80s of no client connection the AI turn was persisted with a real, coherent developmental invitation and no duplicates.

server.py L904-930 (interact endpoint) — properly returns Session immediately after asyncio.create_task; POST latency measured at 0.14s. The 409 guard `if any(t.status=='processing' ...)` correctly prevents duplicate processing turns. The student turn + placeholder are persisted BEFORE create_task, so a race between the two POSTs is impossible.

server.py L944-957 (recover_orphaned_turns) — startup uses `array_filters=[{'t.status': 'processing'}]` with positional operator `turns.$[t].status`, which is the correct MongoDB idiom for updating multiple embedded elements. Note: the ordinary $ positional operator would only update the FIRST processing turn per document; the arrayFilters approach here updates ALL of them. Good.

App.js L54-76 — polling useEffect keys on both session?.id and isProcessing, uses a `cancelled` flag inside the interval, and clears on unmount. The failed-turn toast uses a Ref to avoid re-firing across polls. Initial-load useEffect (L31-48) does NOT need special reconnection handling because it setSession()'s the loaded doc, which sets isProcessing derived state, which triggers the polling useEffect — the reconnection flow is emergent from good state design.

StudentWorkspace.jsx L60-63 — turns filter `!(t.role==='ai' && (t.status==='processing' || t.status==='failed'))` correctly hides placeholder + failed turns from the rendered thread. Combined with the thinking-dot indicator, the UX is coherent.
api.js — interact() is now a plain axios POST; no lingering SSE code. Response type matches the backend Session model.

Startup orphan recovery is a nice safety net (server restart -> any processing turns marked failed), and the failure path in _run_reasoning shares the same terminal state, so the UI toast + retry path is uniform.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Durable processing is now the transport layer for ALL interact requests. Tests should NOT expect SSE anymore — /api/sessions/{id}/interact is a fast JSON POST returning the session (with a processing placeholder), and the client polls GET /api/sessions/{id} every 2.5s until the last AI turn's status flips to 'complete' or 'failed'. For backend correctness, use `_wait_until_idle(sid, max_wait=~220)` — writing turns ~55-70s, revise ~55-90s in normal load, but can spike to 175s+ under LLM contention (see M14 30-case eval). For durability tests, simply don't poll — 80-120s of doing nothing then GET is sufficient. For UI regression, use ?dev bypass and rely on the appearance of [data-testid='ai-invitation'] blocks under the running poller. Startup orphan recovery is verified by code review + main agent already curl-verified; if you want to test it live: submit a turn, then `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` before it completes, then GET the session — the turn should have status='failed'. The 60s SSE ingress ceiling that blocked prior iterations 16-19 is no longer a concern. Public URL: https://dev-converse.preview.emergentagent.com.
rca of the issue: No defects to RCA. The infrastructure change (SSE -> immediate JSON return + background task + client polling) is a clean architectural fix for the prior 60s ingress cutoff and durability gap. Verified: (a) client disconnect during reasoning does NOT tear down the background task because it is decoupled from the request-response lifecycle via asyncio.create_task (not spawned inside a StreamingResponse generator); (b) db.sessions.update_one fires regardless of client presence; (c) the placeholder-turn design gives the UI a clear 'processing' signal without polluting the reasoning view (the reason_session filters the placeholder out at L871); (d) the 409 guard eliminates the previously-possible race of two submissions creating parallel AI turns; (e) startup orphan recovery ensures a server restart cannot leave a session UI hung on a processing indicator.
